summary: Docker Hub limits how many image pulls are allowed from a source, so CI systems and clusters that pull from shared IP addresses can suddenly fail with 'too many requests' errors. This file uses Docker's current documentation, not the 2020 announcement.

overview.background: Docker Hub counts image pulls. Per Docker's current documentation, unauthenticated pulls are limited to 100 per 6 hours per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 subnet, Personal accounts to 200, and paid plans have no pull limit.
systems: CI runners and Kubernetes nodes pulling images
overview.impact: Builds and deployments fail when pulls exceed the limit, for example on shared addresses where many nodes appear as one.
overview.severity: A recurring operational risk rather than a single dated outage.
overview.gaps: This case file describes a mechanism using current docs. It does not describe one specific outage and gives no incident timeline.

archNote: Components and relationships come from the cited source where it describes them. Layout and labels are ours.

diagrams.title: Many nodes behind one address share one budget
diagrams.caption: Per Docker's docs, limits apply per IP address (or IPv6 /64) when unauthenticated. A shared NAT makes many nodes share it.

diagrams.title: Mirror, authenticate, pin (conceptual)
diagrams.caption: General ways to reduce dependence on a public registry.

afterChanges: Builds do not depend on an anonymous public quota.
afterNote: The after picture shows the corrective ideas in the source and general good practice. It is conceptual unless the source says otherwise.
timelineNote: Times are as published by the source. Entries without a clock time are given in order only.

timeline.e: A burst of pulls from one shared address, for example a scaled-up CI run.
Docker Hub returns a rate limit error for further pulls.
Builds fail and logs show a too many requests error.
Engineers check the account, address and the number of pulls.
Authenticate the pulls or point to a mirror or private registry.
Pulls succeed again and builds run.

rootCause.trigger: Pulls from a shared address exceeded the unauthenticated limit.
rootCause.underlying: Docker's documentation sets limits per source address for unauthenticated users.
contributing: Shared NAT egress made many nodes count as one
Images pulled again on every build instead of cached

evidence.label: The documented limits (paraphrased)
evidence.body: Unauthenticated: 100 pulls per 6 hours per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64. Personal: 200. Paid: no pull limit.
evidence.note: A paraphrase of Docker's current documentation, not a verbatim quote. Check the page for current numbers.

evidence.label: A simulated error
evidence.body: toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit.
evidence.note: Typical shape of the message; wording may differ.

diagnose.step: Read the error from the failing pull.
Find the egress address and count pulls.

correct.step: Authenticate pulls with a service account.
correct.why: Raises the limit per Docker's docs.

correct.step: Add a pull-through cache or private registry.

verify.step: Rerun builds and check pulls succeed.

prevent.step: Mirror key images to your own registry.
Pin versions and reduce rebuild pulls.

fix.safety: Do not put registry credentials in logs or public repositories. Use secrets storage.

troubleshoot.scenario: Your CI fails with too many requests errors at the start of the working day. All runners share one egress address.
troubleshoot.question: How do you fix it?
troubleshoot.answer: Authenticate pulls, add a pull-through cache, cache base images and alert on rate-limit errors.

rootcause.q: Why does a shared NAT matter?
options: Limits apply per address for anonymous pulls

remediation.answer: Pull-through cache in your cloud account.
Alert on rate-limit strings in build logs.

design.prompt: Design image supply for a cluster that does not rely on anonymous public pulls.
design.answer: Private registry with replication, signed images, pinned digests, pull-through cache and authentication.

checks.q: What is the unauthenticated limit in the current docs?
options: 100 pulls per 6 hours per IPv4 or IPv6 /64
